thread:
cassie: quick check — i'm planning to bring up a new gpu fleet for a short-lived inference job. want to confirm the TF changes before i open the PR.

jordan: go ahead, drop the snippet here.

cassie: overall plan: a new nodegroup 'workload-gpu-fast' using h100 instances, capacity_reservation for reserved baseline 4 nodes, and a small spot pool for burst. want to make sure metadata & secret wiring is correct.

vikas: sounds reasonable. curious about eni/maxPods and cuda driver sidecar — have you considered p4d vs h100 for the eni limits? h100 8x has similar networking but p4d has a bigger eni footprint.

cassie: good call. i'm using instance_type = "h100-8xlarge" in the TF and set max_pods = 110 to be safe. also adding kubelet extra args to disable gpu-manager preinstall (we handle drivers via DaemonSet).

sam: can you paste the TF snippet? easier to review.

cassie: sure — here's the node group resource:```hcl
resource "aws_eks_node_group" "workload_gpu_fast" {
  cluster_name    = var.cluster
  node_group_name = "workload-gpu-fast"
  node_role_arn   = aws_iam_role.gpu_role.arn
  scaling_config { desired_size = 6; max_size = 12; min_size = 4 }
  instance_types = ["h100-8xlarge"]
  capacity_reservation_options { capacity_reservation_preference = "open" }
  labels = { "node.kubernetes.io/accelerator" = "nvidia" }
  taints = [{ key = "redwood/dedicated" , value = "gpu", effect = "NO_SCHEDULE" }]
  launch_template = { id = aws_launch_template.gpu_lt.id, version = "$Latest" }
}
```

jordan: TF looks fine at a glance. two notes: 1) capacity_reservation_options preference open means it will try open capacity reservations but won't tie to a specific reservation id. if you want guaranteed reserved baseline, add capacity_reservation_targeted or attach reservation id. 2) consider a mixed instances policy for spot fallback.

cassie: yes i'd like guaranteed baseline 4 nodes. any example for targeted reservation in aws?

vikas: we usually create a capacity_reservation resource and then pass capacity_reservation_id to the launch template. like:```hcl
resource "aws_ec2_capacity_reservation" "gpu_baseline" {
  instance_type = "h100-8xlarge"
  availability_zone = "us-west-2a"
  instance_count = 4
  instance_platform = "Linux/UNIX"
}

resource "aws_launch_template" "gpu_lt" {
  # ...
  capacity_reservation_specification { capacity_reservation_preference = "open"; capacity_reservation_target = aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.gpu_baseline.id }
}
```

sam: also reminder: IAM role that the node uses needs ec2:CreateTags and ec2:DescribeCapacityReservations if we target reservation. double-check policies.

cassie: thanks — i'll add that. next question: secrets wiring. the launch template requires an SSM parameter with kubelet bootstrap script and a kms-encrypted key for the instance to fetch private model artifacts. currently we use /redwood/prod/gpu/bootstrap and /redwood/prod/model-key. is that the right pattern?

jordan: prefer storing bootstrap in S3 + signed URL but SSM param is fine for small scripts. ensure the instance profile has kms:Decrypt on the model-key and ssm:GetParameters. Also rotate key id reference in TF to aws_kms_key.model_artifacts.

cassie: noted. i'm also adding a DaemonSet for driver install that reads the model-key from AWS Secrets Manager. snippet:```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: nvidia-driver-installer
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: driver-installer
        image: ourprivreg/driver-bootstrap:stable
        env:
        - name: MODEL_KEY_SECRET
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: gpu-model-key
              key: key
        volumeMounts:
        - name: host-modules
          mountPath: /lib/modules
      volumes:
      - name: host-modules
        hostPath:
          path: /lib/modules
```

vikas: make sure the secret 'gpu-model-key' is created in the cluster or use kube2iam/irsa mapping so the pod can read Secrets Manager directly. we avoid syncing secrets to k8s when they are sensitive.

cassie: we use IRSA for the driver-installer. the pod role policy will call secretsmanager:GetSecretValue. planning to keep k8s secret only for non-sensitive flags.

sam: ops question: rolling strategy — when you scale down due to spot interruption, we should drain gracefully and ensure model cache metrics flush. do we have lifecycle hooks?

cassie: we're adding a termination-handler annotated on nodes and using a node-problem-detector hook to notify cache flusher. plan to set preStop to call /opt/redwood/flush-cache.

infra-bot: terraform plan posted: https://ci.redwood.internal/plan/5678 (applies: 3, changes: 9) :white_check_mark:

cassie: thanks infra-bot. final question — anybody object to enabling kubeletExtraArgs "--evict-hard=imagefs.available<5%" on this group so we don't OOM cache?

jordan: +1 from me.

vikas: +1. also add annotation for node-group to exclude from low-priority autoscaler.

cassie: ok i'll author the PR with the updates: targeted capacity reservation, kms policy, irsa mapping, mixed instances fallback, and the kubelet extra args. will tag you both for review. :thumbsup:
